validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, independent of gem.wiki. This is a real, well-documented Soviet-era trunk line, not a GEM-only entity. Confirmed by: (1) Ukrainian Wikipedia's detailed technical article (route, construction history, compressor station), itself citing primary Ukrainian sources; (2) Ukrtransgaz's own archived corporate history/chronology pages (utg.ua, official Ukrainian TSO predecessor), which name the pipeline explicitly in two separate chronology entries; (3) a 1990s Ukrainian government-era encyclopedia article on pipeline transport (ukrbukva.net, archived) listing it among gas trunklines built/commissioned 1992-1998; (4) a March 2020 Russian public-procurement tender (tenderguru.ru) for decommissioning ('ликвидация') of a specific metering/operator-building site on the pipeline's Russian (Tula-side) segment, contracted by OOO Gazprom Transgaz Moscow -- this independently confirms the physical pipeline's existence on the Russian side as recently as 2020, distinct from and unrelated to gem.wiki. CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as PipelineType=transmission -- Ukrainian sources consistently describe it as a 'магістральний газопровід' (trunk/main gas pipeline) of 1220mm diameter, i.e. large-diameter transmission, not a gathering/feeder line. Fuel=Gas is trivially correct (natural gas trunkline fed by the Yamburg field). DUPLICATE CHECK against the 39-pipeline roster: the pipeline crosses the Russia-Ukraine border in the SAME corridor as the Dashava-Kyiv-Moscow line (P1465), which raised a duplicate flag worth checking -- but Ukrainian Wikipedia explicitly states it diverges eastward after the border, passing through Uhly, Korop, Bakhmach, Mryn and Bobrovytsia (Chernihiv Oblast) before reconverging with the Dashava-Kyiv-Moscow route near Kyiv. This is a documented DISTINCT parallel corridor, not the same physical pipe as P1465 -- no duplicate. Also checked against P0774 'Progress' (also sourced from the Yamburg field, per its FuelSource) -- Progress is the western Urengoy-Uzhgorod II route (1400mm, 4590.7km, via Uzhgorod), a completely different corridor; shared origin field, not a duplicate. No other roster pipeline shares this route or name. Verdict: real, correctly classified, not a duplicate.

validity.recommendation: Optional: add StartYear2=1992 and StartYear3=1995 to reflect the phased commissioning; do not change StartYear1.
validity.researcher_notes: Start year is more nuanced than the single StartYear1=1989 field captures, though 1989 is defensible and not contradicted. Ukrainian Wikipedia (citing a 2016 interview with a Ukrtransgaz official) states construction began in the late 1980s with commissioning 'stretched over 1989-1995'. Ukrtransgaz's own archived corporate chronology page (utg.ua/.../affiliates/kyivtransgas) lists a distinct entry: '1992 р. Введено магістральний газопровід «Тула-Шостка-Київ» діаметром 1220 мм' (1992: commissioned the Tula-Shostka-Kyiv trunk pipeline, 1220mm). A second Ukrtransgaz chronology page (utg.ua/.../xronologya-storichnogo-rozvitku.html) itemizes 136.1 km of the SAME pipeline commissioned specifically in 1995, plus 141.5 km of a communications cable line on the Shostka-Bakhmach-Bobrovytsia section also in 1995. Together these are consistent with a genuinely phased, multi-year build (1989 initial partial commissioning -> 1992 a major commissioning milestone -> 1995 final major segment + ancillary infrastructure), not a contradiction of GEM's StartYear1=1989 -- but a single year cannot represent it fully. Recommend adding StartYear2/StartYear3 rather than treating this as an error.

validity.researcher_notes: Status=operating is correctly retained per country-guidance rule #3 (Russian transit cessation is not grounds to retire a line without dated evidence about THAT line). Two dated, line-specific items are worth flagging without changing the verdict: (1) a March 2020 Russian tender (tenderguru.ru, contracted by OOO Gazprom Transgaz Moscow) for liquidation of the 'PZRG' equipment/operator-building site on this pipeline's Russian (Tula-side) segment; (2) a June 2020 EADaily article (in Russian) confirming Gazprom had begun dismantling its own supply pipes leading to unused sections of the Russia-Ukraine border, as transit consolidated onto fewer entry points (article does not name this pipeline specifically, so it corroborates the general pattern, not this line's fate). Combined with the country-wide facts already established (Sokhranivka entry point closed May 2022; all Russia-Ukraine transit ceased 1 Jan 2025), it is likely this pipeline's original cross-border purpose (moving Yamburg-field gas into Ukraine) is now defunct. However, the pipeline's Ukrainian portion remains part of the domestic GTS -- it connects to the Bobrovytska compressor station (commissioned 2008) and the Chervonopartyzanske underground gas storage facility, both of which support ongoing domestic transmission/storage cycling independent of cross-border imports. Owner1='Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' (TSOU) is confirmed as Ukraine's real, current (since 1 Jan 2020) certified GTS operator by TSOU's own official 'Key Facts' page (archived, verified live wording: 'Starting from January 1, 2020, LLC Gas TSO of Ukraine is the certified operator of the gas transmission system of Ukraine'). Owner2='Gazprom PJSC' is independently corroborated for the RUSSIAN segment specifically by the same tenderguru.ru tender, which names OOO Gazprom Transgaz Moscow (a Gazprom subsidiary) as the contracting entity responsible for facilities on this exact pipeline's Russian side. This is the correct cross-border split per country guidance (Gazprom owns nothing in Ukraine; the Ukrainian section is the Ukrainian state's) -- both owners are well-supported and should NOT be collapsed to one.

fills.researcher_notes: Status inferred from context, not a literal status word: both sources describe the pipeline as a functioning part of Ukraine's operating trunk gas network (with an active compressor station added in 2008), consistent with 'operating'. No dated evidence found that the physical Ukrainian asset itself has been retired; see validity notes on the cross-border-flow caveat.
Article explicitly describes it as a natural-gas trunkline ('газопровід') carrying gas from the Yamburg gas-condensate field.
Both sources describe it as a 'магістральний газопровід' (trunk/main gas pipeline), i.e. transmission, consistent with its 1220mm large diameter.

Ukrtransgaz's own archived corporate chronology states explicitly: '1992 р. Введено магістральний газопровід «Тула-Шостка-Київ» діаметром 1220 мм' (diameter 1220mm), exact match to GEM. Ukrainian Wikipedia's diameter figure traces to this same UTG page (shared origin, not a second independent source), so tier is medium (1 strong primary/official source) rather than high.

Archived Ukrainian article on pipeline transport lists gas trunklines commissioned in the 1990s and states 'Тула-Шостка-Київ (490 км)' -- exact match to GEM's 490.00 km. Single strong source found (a second explicit total-length figure could not be located independently within available time); tier medium.
Article states construction of this pipeline is directly tied to development of the Yamburg gas-condensate field in Tyumen Oblast, Russia -- exact match to GEM's FuelSource=Yamburg.

Confirms Tula (Tula Oblast, Russia) as the origin hub (where the North Caucasus-Center corridor passes and the Yamburg-Tula pipeline terminates) and Kyiv as the destination, crossing the Russia-Ukraine border then routing through Chernihiv Oblast (Uhly, Korop, Bakhmach, Mryn, Bobrovytsia) toward Kyiv.

summary: P1455 (Tula-Shostka-Kiev): existence, classification (transmission) and duplicate status all confirmed via independent Ukrainian/Russian sources -- real, distinct from P1465's parallel Dashava-Kyiv-Moscow corridor; length 490km and diameter 1220mm corroborated; Start=1989 defensible but reflects only the first of three documented phased-commissioning years (1989/1992/1995); cross-border Owner1=TSOU / Owner2=Gazprom split independently confirmed as correct; caveat noted (not a status change) re: a 2020 Gazprom tender to decommission Russian-side metering equipment amid the broader cessation of Russia-Ukraine transit.
